compiled_state.title: As a DSO sprint operator, I want design-md-lint.sh enforced in Sprint Phase F and eligible for FP-recovery, so that design-system violations are caught during sprint execution and false positives can be escaped.
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Wires design-md-lint.sh into Sprint Phase F enforcement and FP-recovery escape path.
**Why**: Pre-commit enforcement alone is insufficient — sprint sub-agents bypass hooks. Sprint Phase F integration catches violations during orchestrated execution.
**Scope**:
- IN: Sprint Phase F lint step (shared-directory and worktree-isolation modes), FP-recovery DESIGN.md lint finding eligibility
- OUT: Pre-commit hook (draft-2), preplanning flow (draft-5)

## Done Definitions

- Sprint Phase F runs design-md-lint.sh against the batch's touched files between Step 11 and Step 12 in shared-directory mode and blocks the batch on violations ← Satisfies: sc-3 (sc-3: "Sprint and FP-recovery enforcement integration")
- Sprint Phase F runs design-md-lint.sh at the equivalent enforcement point in per-worktree-review-commit.md (worktree-isolation mode) and blocks the batch on violations ← Satisfies: sc-3
- /dso:fp-recovery accepts DESIGN.md lint findings as eligible false-positive escape candidates using the same workflow it uses for code-reviewer findings ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Ordering] The lint step must run after code changes are applied (Step 11) but before the review gate (Step 12) to catch violations before they reach the reviewer.
- [FP-recovery] The FP-recovery integration should reuse existing finding classification infrastructure rather than duplicating it.
- [Integration] FP-recovery currently operates on CI llm-review findings (reviewer-findings.json). DESIGN.md lint findings come from a different tool with a different output format. Specify: (a) what format design-md-lint.sh findings must be in for FP-recovery to consume them, (b) whether FP-recovery needs to be modified to recognize a new finding source.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
